note: Frame selection is inherently non-deterministic and slot-exact agreement is the wrong metric. Re-running the identical pipeline over the identical cached frames changed 5/35 picks at temperature 0.2 and 7/40 at temperature 0 — the serving stack, not the sampling temperature, is the source. The score swung 68.6% <-> 77.1% with no code change, which is wider than most improvements measured so far. Every one of the 7 flipped guides was a flip between two frames that the (human-calibrated) verification prompt accepts, so the instability is benign: both frames show what the guide asks for. Slot-exact agreement penalises benign variation because the human only ever judged the single frame that was shown to them.

pick_instability.conclusion: temperature is not the cause; do not ship a temperature change

flip_quality.checked_with: 2026-08-03 revised verification prompt (0 false rejections on 34 human-judged frames)

metric.retire: slot-exact agreement against a single judged frame
metric.adopt: wrong photos delivered (target 0) + correct photo vs link fallback
metric.sample_status: 0 wrong photos delivered across the 35 judged guides; 2 fall back to a link where a valid frame existed

sampling.note: 35 guides cannot resolve 99% — one error is 2.9 points and run-to-run noise is ~9. A 99% claim needs a larger batch and judgements on all three candidates, not one.
